label: 4th original token after a [u/w/q/b][v/d][v/d] prefix (e.g. "w v d h")
explanation: Very sparse feature that fires only in the original phase, almost always at t=3 (95% of mass; a few at t=4). It is a conjunction over the specific prefix: the first token is u or w (sometimes q or b), tokens 1 and 2 are each v or d (e.g. u v v, w v d, u d v), and the current input is one of w/h/s/3/u/y/c. The strongest activations come from the exact u/w + {v,d}{v,d} prefix with input s/w/h. Weaker activations happen when one prefix slot is a near-match (y, w, n, x in place of v/d, or the pattern shifted to t=4 as in u d v d h / u w v d h) or the input is 2/o/p. Activation is fairly flat (0.10-0.15). It never fires at the delimiter or during the copy phase, and never at t<3. The conjunction predicate gets dev F1 about 0.68. With first token u/w only, precision is about 0.97 but recall is about 0.49, so the feature behaves like a soft match on this particular token trigram plus the next token.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 27 cues. Raise it: t=3 & prev_tok=v (+2.62), t=3 & prev_tok=d (+2.33), orig0=u (+2.14), prev2_tok=v (+2.06), prev_tok=d (+1.96), prev3_tok=w (+1.90). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-1.98), in_count=1 (-0.96), orig7=- (-0.64).
